ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there is a tri-state gate function block, marked with “&” inside the block, indicating that the inside is an AND gate function; on the left side there are two data input terminals A and B connected to this function block; at the lower left there is also an enable terminal, labeled EN, and this terminal is connected to logic 1; the output terminal on the right leads to F, and there is a small circle at the output terminal position, indicating output inversion. Reasoning: Because EN is connected to logic 1, the tri-state gate is enabled, and the output is not in a high-impedance state. The internal “&” gate first obtains the result of A AND B, namely A·B; the small circle at the output terminal indicates taking the inversion of this result, so F equals the inverse of A·B. Final answer: \(F=\overline{A\cdot B}\).
